claims.evidence: The UK receipt mentioned was not shown in the report.
No photo of the system software version or the home screen showing installed games.
Photo 0 shows two controllers in retail packaging.
The warranty seal/sticker on the rear of the console was not shown.
Thermal performance cannot be determined from static photos.
Port functionality requires physical testing or a video of peripherals connected.

risks.risk: The console may have the base 500GB storage rather than 1TB.
risks.proof: A photo of the 'System Storage' menu in settings.

risks.risk: The console might not be 'hacked' (requires firmware 9.00 or 11.00 or lower).
risks.proof: A photo of the 'System Information' screen showing the firmware version.

risks.risk: The console may have been opened or repaired despite claims.
risks.proof: A clear close-up of the black plastic warranty seal over the screw hole on the back.

risks.risk: The console may be banned from PSN or have a faulty disc drive/APU (BLOD).
risks.proof: A video showing the console booting to the dashboard and launching a game.

proof_requests: Photo of the System Information screen showing firmware version and storage capacity.
Photo of the rear of the console showing the model number and the warranty seal.
Photo of the UK receipt mentioned by the seller.
Video of the console powered on and running a game.
response.reason: The witness has confirmed the identity as a PS4 Slim with two boxed controllers, allowing for a baseline valuation at the lowest storage capacity and unverified firmware status.
